what: The apparatus a leaf may show around a thin record: where its name stands in the corpus, where the texts disagree about it, its genealogy, what it is attested beside, and -- named, not implied -- what was searched for and not found. Ruling C10 of 19 August 2026, step 1: pull in more archive before art, before the declared silence, before letting the book be thinner.
how: Every corpus question goes through map/ardatext.py, the archive's one matcher, because the corpus is stored in MIXED Unicode normalisation and a raw search for a composed Théoden finds 0 of the 261 that stand in The Lord of the Rings. Names are matched as TOKEN SEQUENCES over ardatext.fold(line, keep_case=True) -- the word-boundary path -- never as substrings over a squeezed stream, which reports a name inside unrelated words. Case and accents are kept, so Dale the town is separable from dale the valley.
conf_note: A marker here grades WHAT THE ATTESTATION IS WORTH AS A WITNESS, not what the record is worth as canon. [C] means the name stands in a text of Tolkien's own, decided from site/arda_sources.json's tier and primary_text fields and not from a reading of this module; [EXT] means it stands in someone else's book about him. It does NOT say the line is about this record: a name standing in a line is a fact about the line, and a reader can check it because the line is printed here.
silence_note: A silence in this file was SEARCHED. Every `silence` entry names the question, the population it was asked over, and the count that came back. Where nothing was searched the entry says NOT SEARCHED and why -- the owner's ruling of 12 August: a silence may only be asserted by something that looked.

refuses.aboutness: It does not decide whether a corpus line is ABOUT the record whose name stands in it, and it never will. Pronouns are not resolved, so a figure discussed for a page under `he` is attested once.
refuses.shortened probes that more than one reco: A probe shorter than a record's name -- its head-word, its half of a compound, the name inside its own parentheses -- is used only where exactly ONE record in this archive answers to it. Barahir (Faramir's grandson) is not probed as `Barahir`, because Beren's father has his own leaf; Míriel Serindë is not probed as `Míriel`, because Tar-Míriel exists. Each refusal is recorded as a NOT SEARCHED silence naming the form and the count that refused it. Handing one Míriel the other's lines would be an invented attribution wearing a citation.
refuses.a place's generic head-word: Ered is `mountains`, Dor is `land`, Sarn is `stone`; in English, Sea, Lake, Isle, Tower and Havens are the same. Each is refused by COUNTING, not by a rule about what kind of record it is: every one of them heads several names this archive holds, so the onomasticon test refuses it. The first build had no such test and gave Sea of Rhûn 3,216 lines about the Great Sea.
refuses.unregistered volumes: A corpus file with no entry in site/arda_sources.json gets no marker on its attestations rather than a guessed one.

oaths.q:
Then Fëanor swore a terrible oath. His seven sons leapt straightway to his side and took the selfsame vow together, and red as blood shone their drawn swords in the glare of the torches. They swore an oath which none shall break, and none should take, by the name even of Ilúvatar, calling the Everlasting Dark upon them if they kept it not; and Manwë they named in witness, and Varda, and the hallowed mountain of Taniquetil, vowing to pursue with vengeance and hatred to the ends of the World Vala, Demon, Elf or Man as yet unborn, or any creature, great or small, good or evil, that time should bring forth unto the end of days, whoso should hold or take or keep a Silmaril from their possession.

Thus spoke Maedhros and Maglor and Celegorm, Curufin and Caranthir, Amrod and Amras, princes of the Noldor; and many quailed to hear the dread words. For so sworn, good or evil, an oath may not be broken, and it shall pursue oathkeeper and oathbreaker to the world's end.

Then Fëanor swore a terrible oath. His seven sons leapt straightway to his side and took the selfsame vow together, and red as blood shone their drawn swords in the glare of the torches. They swore an oath which none shall break, and none should take, by the name even of Ilúvatar, calling the Everlasting Dark upon them if they kept it not; and Manwë they named in witness, and Varda, and the hallowed mountain of Taniquetil, vowing to pursue with vengeance and hatred to the ends of the World Vala, Demon, Elf or Man as yet unborn, or any creature, great or small, good or evil, that time should bring forth unto the end of days, whoso should hold or take or keep a Silmaril from their possession.

Thus spoke Maedhros and Maglor and Celegorm, Curufin and Caranthir, Amrod and Amras, princes of the Noldor; and many quailed to hear the dread words. For so sworn, good or evil, an oath may not be broken, and it shall pursue oathkeeper and oathbreaker to the world's end.

oaths.when: F.o.A. 120 (S.R. 1541), Mar 1, in the House of the Kings, Minas Tirith
oaths.q:
'Lady Undómiel,' said Aragorn, 'the hour is indeed hard, yet it was made even in that day when we met under the white birches in the garden of Elrond where none now walk. And on the hill of Cerin Amroth when we forsook both the Shadow and the Twilight this doom we accepted… I am the last of the Númenóreans and the latest King of the Elder Days; and to me has been given not only a span thrice that of Men of Middle-earth, but also the grace to go at my will, and give back the gift. Now, therefore, I will sleep.
   'I speak no comfort to you, for there is no comfort for such pain within the circles of the world. The uttermost choice is before you: to repent and go to the Havens and bear away into the West the memory of our days together that shall there be evergreen but never more than memory; or else to abide the Doom of Men.'
    'Nay, dear lord,' she said, 'that choice is long over. There is now no ship that would bear me hence, and I must indeed abide the Doom of Men, whether I will or I nill: the loss and the silence… For if this is indeed, as the Eldar say, the gift of the One to Men, it is bitter to receive.'
    'So it seems,' he said. 'But let us not be overthrown at the final test, who of old renounced the Shadow and the Ring. In sorrow we must go, but not in despair. Behold! we are not bound for ever to the circles of the world, and beyond them is more than memory. Farewell!'
    'Estel, Estel!' she cried

oaths.cite: LotR Appendix A I(v), 'The Tale of Aragorn and Arwen', for the words [C]; LotR Appendix B, the Tale of Years of the Fourth Age, for the YEAR [C] — 'came at last the Passing of King Elessar' (t1_c_the_lord_of_the_rings.txt:49384). THE LABEL READ 'F.A. 120' AND F.A. IS THE FIRST AGE IN THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN VOCABULARY, which would place Aragorn's death some seven thousand years before he was born, between Turgon's coming to Nevrast and the Nirnaeth. The Fourth Age is spelled F.o.A. here — arda_chronology already carries this same event as 'F.o.A. 120 (S.R. 1541), Mar 1'. AND APPENDIX A DOES NOT DATE IT: the Tale of Aragorn and Arwen carries ZERO occurrences of 'Fourth Age' and no year at all; Appendix B's Shire-Reckoning column is the annal. Eleventh instance of citing Appendix A, the narrative genealogy, where Appendix B, the annal, holds the date — after 426, 433, 434, 437-439 and belegost CORRECTED 19 Aug 2026: this field quoted the annal as '1541 In this year on March 1st came at last the Passing of King Elessar'. THE BOOK PRINTS 'In this year1' -- a footnote marker fused into the word -- so the tidied string verifies NOWHERE in tier 1 and verified only in t2_the_lord_of_the_rings_a_reader_s_companion.txt, a tier 2 reprint that drops the marker. A tier 1 claim was resting on a tier 2 reproduction. The quotation is shortened to the span the book itself prints; the year 1541 is unchanged and is what the annal states.

oaths.q: he swore an oath of abiding friendship and aid in every need to Barahir and all his kin, and in token of his vow he gave to Barahir his ring.
oaths.name: Finrod Felagund's oath to Barahir
oaths.cite: HoME XI, the Grey Annals §146, year header 455 [C] — 'Then Inglor gave to Barahir his ring, an heirloom of his house, in token of the oath that he swore unto Barahir'. NOT 460: the 460 annal (§§163-164) covers Barahir's outlawry and death and contains no oath. The annal names the giver INGLOR; 'Finrod' in the Grey Annals is his FATHER, Finarfin. Header verified by me.

oaths.q: 'I see the ring, son of Barahir, and I perceive that you are proud, and deem yourself mighty. But a father's deeds, even had his service been rendered to me, avail not to win the daughter of Thingol and Melian. See now! I too desire a treasure that is withheld. For rock and steel and the fires of Morgoth keep the jewel that I would possess against all the powers of the Elf-kingdoms. Yet I hear you say that bonds such as these do not daunt you. Go your way therefore! Bring to me in your hand a Silmaril from Morgoth's crown; and then, if she will, Lúthien may set her hand in yours. Then you shall have my jewel; and though the fate of Arda lie within the Silmarils, yet you shall hold me generous.'
oaths.name: Thingol's demand for a Silmaril
oaths.cite: Silm 19 for the words [C]; GA 465 §178 (Version I) and §189 (Version II), HoME XI [C] for the YEAR AND THE EVENT — V II §189, the demand in direct speech: "'If thou fearest neither spell, wall nor weapons, as thou saist, then go fetch me a Silmaril from the crown of Morgoth. Then we will give jewel for jewel, but thou shalt win the fairer: Lúthien of the First-born and of the Gods.'" V I §178 gives it in report, and the verifying span is 'a Silmaril from the crown of Morgoth as the bride-price of Lúthien' — the words before it read 'he must bririg', WHICH IS THE CORPUS'S OWN OCR CORRUPTION OF 'bring' and is left out of the quotation rather than silently corrected: quoted_check refused the corrected form, which is the guard working. RECENSION NAMED. The annal's wording is not the Silmarillion's: 'Bring to me in your hand a Silmaril' is ABSENT from the Grey Annals

oaths.q: 'For little price,' he said, 'do Elven-kings sell their daughters: for gems, and things made by craft. But if this be your will, Thingol, I will perform it. And when we meet again my hand shall hold a Silmaril from the Iron Crown; for you have not looked the last upon Beren son of Barahir.'
oaths.name: Beren's oath to Thingol
oaths.cite: Silm 19 for the words [C]. THE EVENT IS ANNALLED AND THE WORDING IS NOT, and the division is the point of this cite. GA 465 dates the audience at Menegroth and Beren's taking of the Quest — §190 (Version II): 'he took upon himself the Quest of the Silmaril, and went forth from Menegroth alone', and §178 (Version I): 'But Beren took the quest upon himself and departed'. BOTH ARE WORDLESS. The annal DOES carry an oath of Beren's at 465, §189, but it is a DIFFERENT OATH sworn BEFORE the Silmaril is named — 'swore that by no power of spell, wall or weapon should he be withheld from his love'. The archive's answering vow appears in NO annal in Beren's own mouth; it survives only as Thingol's back-reference under 466, §209: 'Didst thou not say that thou wouldst not return to me save with a jewel from the crown of Morgoth?' [I-M] on the attribution of these words to F.A. 465: the annal asserts the promise was made and never shows it being made

oaths.q: 'I see the ring, son of Barahir, and I perceive that you are proud, and deem yourself mighty. But a father's deeds, even had his service been rendered to me, avail not to win the daughter of Thingol and Melian. See now! I too desire a treasure that is withheld. For rock and steel and the fires of Morgoth keep the jewel that I would possess against all the powers of the Elf-kingdoms. Yet I hear you say that bonds such as these do not daunt you. Go your way therefore! Bring to me in your hand a Silmaril from Morgoth's crown; and then, if she will, Lúthien may set her hand in yours. Then you shall have my jewel; and though the fate of Arda lie within the Silmarils, yet you shall hold me generous.'
oaths.name: Thingol's demand for a Silmaril
oaths.cite: Silm 19 for the words [C]; GA 465 §178 (Version I) and §189 (Version II), HoME XI [C] for the YEAR AND THE EVENT — V II §189, the demand in direct speech: "'If thou fearest neither spell, wall nor weapons, as thou saist, then go fetch me a Silmaril from the crown of Morgoth. Then we will give jewel for jewel, but thou shalt win the fairer: Lúthien of the First-born and of the Gods.'" V I §178 gives it in report, and the verifying span is 'a Silmaril from the crown of Morgoth as the bride-price of Lúthien' — the words before it read 'he must bririg', WHICH IS THE CORPUS'S OWN OCR CORRUPTION OF 'bring' and is left out of the quotation rather than silently corrected: quoted_check refused the corrected form, which is the guard working. RECENSION NAMED. The annal's wording is not the Silmarillion's: 'Bring to me in your hand a Silmaril' is ABSENT from the Grey Annals

oaths.q: 'For little price,' he said, 'do Elven-kings sell their daughters: for gems, and things made by craft. But if this be your will, Thingol, I will perform it. And when we meet again my hand shall hold a Silmaril from the Iron Crown; for you have not looked the last upon Beren son of Barahir.'
oaths.name: Beren's oath to Thingol
oaths.cite: Silm 19 for the words [C]. THE EVENT IS ANNALLED AND THE WORDING IS NOT, and the division is the point of this cite. GA 465 dates the audience at Menegroth and Beren's taking of the Quest — §190 (Version II): 'he took upon himself the Quest of the Silmaril, and went forth from Menegroth alone', and §178 (Version I): 'But Beren took the quest upon himself and departed'. BOTH ARE WORDLESS. The annal DOES carry an oath of Beren's at 465, §189, but it is a DIFFERENT OATH sworn BEFORE the Silmaril is named — 'swore that by no power of spell, wall or weapon should he be withheld from his love'. The archive's answering vow appears in NO annal in Beren's own mouth; it survives only as Thingol's back-reference under 466, §209: 'Didst thou not say that thou wouldst not return to me save with a jewel from the crown of Morgoth?' [I-M] on the attribution of these words to F.A. 465: the annal asserts the promise was made and never shows it being made

oaths.q:
But Beren knelt before him, and said: 'I return according to my word. I am come now to claim my own.'
    And Thingol answered: 'What of your quest, and of your vow?'
    But Beren said: 'It is fulfilled. Even now a Silmaril is in my hand.'
    Then Thingol said: 'Show it to me!'
   And Beren put forth his left hand, slowly opening its fingers; but it was empty. Then he held up his right arm; and from that hour he named himself Camlost, the Empty-handed.
oaths.name: 'Even now a Silmaril is in my hand'
oaths.cite: Silm 19 for the words [C]; GA 466 §209, HoME XI [C] for the YEAR AND THE WORDS, WHICH SURVIVE VERBATIM HERE where nothing else in this group does — 'And Beren answered: "Even now a Silmaril is in my hand." And Thingol said: "Show it to me!" But Beren said: "That I cannot do; for my hand is not here." And he held up his right arm; and from that hour he named himself Camlost'. VERSION II ONLY, AND THAT MATTERS: Version I's annal 466 (§185) records the return and the betrothal and OMITS the naming entirely. The epithet is separately annalled at Beren's birth, GA 432 §139: 'who was after named Erchamion the One-handed and Camlost the Emptyhanded'

oaths.q:
Then Fëanor swore a terrible oath. His seven sons leapt straightway to his side and took the selfsame vow together, and red as blood shone their drawn swords in the glare of the torches. They swore an oath which none shall break, and none should take, by the name even of Ilúvatar, calling the Everlasting Dark upon them if they kept it not; and Manwë they named in witness, and Varda, and the hallowed mountain of Taniquetil, vowing to pursue with vengeance and hatred to the ends of the World Vala, Demon, Elf or Man as yet unborn, or any creature, great or small, good or evil, that time should bring forth unto the end of days, whoso should hold or take or keep a Silmaril from their possession.

Thus spoke Maedhros and Maglor and Celegorm, Curufin and Caranthir, Amrod and Amras, princes of the Noldor; and many quailed to hear the dread words. For so sworn, good or evil, an oath may not be broken, and it shall pursue oathkeeper and oathbreaker to the world's end.

oaths.q:
Then Fëanor swore a terrible oath. His seven sons leapt straightway to his side and took the selfsame vow together, and red as blood shone their drawn swords in the glare of the torches. They swore an oath which none shall break, and none should take, by the name even of Ilúvatar, calling the Everlasting Dark upon them if they kept it not; and Manwë they named in witness, and Varda, and the hallowed mountain of Taniquetil, vowing to pursue with vengeance and hatred to the ends of the World Vala, Demon, Elf or Man as yet unborn, or any creature, great or small, good or evil, that time should bring forth unto the end of days, whoso should hold or take or keep a Silmaril from their possession.

Thus spoke Maedhros and Maglor and Celegorm, Curufin and Caranthir, Amrod and Amras, princes of the Noldor; and many quailed to hear the dread words. For so sworn, good or evil, an oath may not be broken, and it shall pursue oathkeeper and oathbreaker to the world's end.
oaths.name: The Oath of Fëanor
oaths.cite: HoME X, the Annals of Aman §134, year header 1495 [C] — 'Then Feanor swore a terrible oath. Straightway his seven sons leaped to his side and each took the selfsame oath'. CONFIRMED at Y.T. 1495, header verified by me. The alliterative verse is INSIDE this annal, not a variant beside it.

oaths.q: 'Be he friend or foe, whether demon of Morgoth, or Elf, or child of Men, or any other living thing in Arda, neither law, nor love, nor league of hell, nor might of the Valar, nor any power of wizardry, shall defend him from the pursuing hate of Fëanor's sons, if he take or find a Silmaril and keep it. For the Silmarils we alone claim, until the world ends.'
oaths.name: Celegorm's re-swearing of the Oath in Nargothrond
oaths.cite: Silm 19 for the words [C]; GA 465 §193, Version II (HoME XI) [C] for the YEAR AND THE EVENT — Celegorn to Felagund: 'Know this: thy going is vain; for could ye achieve this quest it would avail nothing. Neither thee nor this Man should we suffer to keep or to give a Silmaril of Fëanor. Against thee would come all the brethren to slay thee rather. And should Thingol gain it, then we would burn Doriath or die in the attempt. For we have sworn our Oath.' Header verified by me in the Grey Annals section: 465. RECENSION NAMED — Version II; the Grey Annals print two 465s. THE ANNAL CARRIES THE INVOCATION AND NOT THE OATH'S TEXT: the words this record quotes are the Oath of Fëanor itself, sworn in Y.T. 1495, and what the annal shows is Celegorn invoking it at Nargothrond — 'For we have sworn our Oath'. Note the annal spells him Celegorn, not Celegorm

oaths.q:
It is told among the Elves that after Eärendil had departed, seeking Elwing his wife, Mandos spoke concerning his fate; and he said: 'Shall mortal Man step living upon the undying lands, and yet live?' But Ulmo said: 'For this he was born into the world. And say unto me: whether is he Eärendil Tuor's son of the line of Hador, or the son of Idril, Turgon's daughter, of the Elven-house of Finwë?' And Mandos answered: 'Equally the Noldor, who went wilfully into exile, may not return hither.'
    But when all was spoken, Manwë gave judgement, and he said: 'In this matter the power of doom is given to me. The peril that he ventured for love of the Two Kindreds shall not fall upon Eärendil, nor shall it fall upon Elwing his wife, who entered into peril for love of him; but they shall not walk again ever among Elves or Men in the Outer Lands. And this is my decree concerning them: to Eärendil and to Elwing, and to their sons, shall be given leave each to choose freely to which kindred their fates shall be joined, and under which kindred they shall be judged.'
oaths.name: The errand of Eärendil and the judgement of Manwë
oaths.cite: Silm 24 for the words [C]; HoME XI, the TALE OF YEARS, recension C [C] for the YEAR — the entry reads '536 [> 540 > 542] Earendil comes to Valinor', the bracketed chain being Tolkien's own manuscript emendations as Christopher prints them; recension B reports the same movement, 'The date of Ëarendil's coming to Valinor was changed several times, apparently > 536 > 540 > 542', and recension A's original entry is '533 Earendil comes to Valinor'. I read all three at their lines rather than through map/annal_header.py, WHICH RETURNS A WRONG HEADER HERE: its inline pattern requires a digit followed by whitespace and a capital, so '536 [> 540 > 542]' never matches and the entry falls into the previous block — the tool answers 503/533. THE GREY ANNALS CANNOT DATE THIS: they end at 499, inside Túrin's death annal, 'Here the manuscript comes to an end, at the foot of a page, and the typescript also'. AB 2 gives 533 instead, unemended. AND THE ANNAL DATES THE COMING, NOT THE ERRAND: no annal in any tradition carries the errand-speech or Manwë's judgement

oaths.q:
'The others go with him as free companions, to help him on his way. You may tarry, or come back, or turn aside into other paths, as chance allows. The further you go, the less easy will it be to withdraw; yet no oath or bond is laid on you to go further than you will. For you do not yet know the strength of your hearts, and you cannot foresee what each may meet upon the road.'
    'Faithless is he that says farewell when the road darkens,' said Gimli.
    'Maybe,' said Elrond, 'but let him not vow to walk in the dark, who has not seen the nightfall.'
    'Yet sworn word may strengthen quaking heart,' said Gimli.
    'Or break it,' said Elrond.

oaths.q:
It is told among the Elves that after Eärendil had departed, seeking Elwing his wife, Mandos spoke concerning his fate; and he said: 'Shall mortal Man step living upon the undying lands, and yet live?' But Ulmo said: 'For this he was born into the world. And say unto me: whether is he Eärendil Tuor's son of the line of Hador, or the son of Idril, Turgon's daughter, of the Elven-house of Finwë?' And Mandos answered: 'Equally the Noldor, who went wilfully into exile, may not return hither.'
    But when all was spoken, Manwë gave judgement, and he said: 'In this matter the power of doom is given to me. The peril that he ventured for love of the Two Kindreds shall not fall upon Eärendil, nor shall it fall upon Elwing his wife, who entered into peril for love of him; but they shall not walk again ever among Elves or Men in the Outer Lands. And this is my decree concerning them: to Eärendil and to Elwing, and to their sons, shall be given leave each to choose freely to which kindred their fates shall be joined, and under which kindred they shall be judged.'
oaths.name: The errand of Eärendil and the judgement of Manwë
oaths.cite: Silm 24 for the words [C]; HoME XI, the TALE OF YEARS, recension C [C] for the YEAR — the entry reads '536 [> 540 > 542] Earendil comes to Valinor', the bracketed chain being Tolkien's own manuscript emendations as Christopher prints them; recension B reports the same movement, 'The date of Ëarendil's coming to Valinor was changed several times, apparently > 536 > 540 > 542', and recension A's original entry is '533 Earendil comes to Valinor'. I read all three at their lines rather than through map/annal_header.py, WHICH RETURNS A WRONG HEADER HERE: its inline pattern requires a digit followed by whitespace and a capital, so '536 [> 540 > 542]' never matches and the entry falls into the previous block — the tool answers 503/533. THE GREY ANNALS CANNOT DATE THIS: they end at 499, inside Túrin's death annal, 'Here the manuscript comes to an end, at the foot of a page, and the typescript also'. AB 2 gives 533 instead, unemended. AND THE ANNAL DATES THE COMING, NOT THE ERRAND: no annal in any tradition carries the errand-speech or Manwë's judgement

oaths.when: T.A. 2510, on the Halifirien at the tomb of Elendil
oaths.q: Hear now all peoples who bow not to the Shadow in the East, by the gift of the Lord of the Mundburg we will come to dwell in the land that he names Calenardhon, and therefore I vow in my own name and on behalf of the Éothéod of the North that between us and the Great People of the West there shall be friendship for ever: their enemies shall be our enemies, their need shall be our need, and whatsoever evil, or threat, or assault may come upon them we will aid them to the utmost end of our strength. This vow shall descend to my heirs, all such as may come after me in our new land, and let them keep it in faith unbroken, lest the Shadow fall upon them and they become accursed.
oaths.name: The Oath of Eorl
oaths.cite: UT III.ii, 'Cirion and Eorl', for the words — 'there shall be friendship for ever' [C]. UT SUPPLIES THE YEAR, and for the BATTLE AND THE GRANT rather than the oath itself: 'the victory of Eorl on the Field of Celebrant in the year 2510' and 'granted Calenardhon to the Rohirrim after the Battle of the Field of Celebrant in Third Age 2510' (UT, Index, s.v. Cirion). The oath accompanies the grant. NO ANNAL: 'Cirion' and 'oath' each occur ZERO times in LotR Appendix B, whose 2510 entry names the victory and the settlement and no oath. Both counts verified by me. [I-M] ON THE YEAR: NO ANNAL DATES EITHER OATH. 'Cirion' and 'oath' each occur ZERO times in Appendix B, verified by me, and its 2510 entry names the victory and the settlement and no oath. UT supplies the year for the BATTLE and the GRANT, and the oath accompanies the grant — which is a reading, not a witness.

oaths.q:
Then Fëanor swore a terrible oath. His seven sons leapt straightway to his side and took the selfsame vow together, and red as blood shone their drawn swords in the glare of the torches. They swore an oath which none shall break, and none should take, by the name even of Ilúvatar, calling the Everlasting Dark upon them if they kept it not; and Manwë they named in witness, and Varda, and the hallowed mountain of Taniquetil, vowing to pursue with vengeance and hatred to the ends of the World Vala, Demon, Elf or Man as yet unborn, or any creature, great or small, good or evil, that time should bring forth unto the end of days, whoso should hold or take or keep a Silmaril from their possession.

Thus spoke Maedhros and Maglor and Celegorm, Curufin and Caranthir, Amrod and Amras, princes of the Noldor; and many quailed to hear the dread words. For so sworn, good or evil, an oath may not be broken, and it shall pursue oathkeeper and oathbreaker to the world's end.
oaths.name: The Oath of Fëanor
oaths.cite: HoME X, the Annals of Aman §134, year header 1495 [C] — 'Then Feanor swore a terrible oath. Straightway his seven sons leaped to his side and each took the selfsame oath'. CONFIRMED at Y.T. 1495, header verified by me. The alliterative verse is INSIDE this annal, not a variant beside it.

oaths.q:
'Be he foe or friend, be he foul or clean,
brood of Morgoth or bright Vala,
Elda or Maia or Aftercomer,
Man yet unborn upon Middle-earth,
neither law, nor love, nor league of swords,
dread nor danger, not Doom itself,
shall defend him from Fëanor, and Fëanor's kin,
whoso hideth or hoardeth, or in hand taketh,
finding keepeth or afar casteth
a Silmaril. This swear we all:
death we will deal him ere Day's ending,
woe unto world's end! Our word hear thou,
Eru Allfather! To the everlasting
Darkness doom us if our deed faileth.
On the holy mountain hear in witness
and our vow remember, Manwë and Varda!'
oaths.name: The Oath of Fëanor (verse form, Annals of Aman)
oaths.cite: HoME X, Annals of Aman §134

oaths.q:
'Be he friend or foe or foul offspring
of Morgoth Bauglir, be he mortal dark
that in after days on earth shall dwell,
shall no law nor love nor league of Gods,
no might nor mercy, not moveless fate,
defend him for ever from the fierce vengeance
of the sons of Feanor, whoso seize or steal
or finding keep the fair enchanted
globes of crystal whose glory dies not,
the Silmarils. We have sworn for ever!'
oaths.name: The Oath of Fëanor (alliterative, The Flight of the Noldoli)
oaths.cite: HoME III, The Flight of the Noldoli, for the alliterative text; HoME X, the Annals of Aman §134, year header 1495 [C] for the year — AND THE VERSE IS INSIDE THAT ANNAL, not a variant beside it: §134 gives 'Then Feanor swore a terrible oath' and then the sixteen alliterative lines entire. Header verified by me with map/annal_header.py.

oaths.q: 'Tears unnumbered ye shall shed; and the Valar will fence Valinor against you, and shut you out, so that not even the echo of your lamentation shall pass over the mountains. On the House of Fëanor the wrath of the Valar lieth from the West unto the uttermost East, and upon all that will follow them it shall be laid also. Their Oath shall drive them, and yet betray them, and ever snatch away the very treasures that they have sworn to pursue. To evil end shall all things turn that they begin well; and by treason of kin unto kin, and the fear of treason, shall this come to pass. The Dispossessed shall they be for ever.'
oaths.name: The Prophecy of the North (the Doom of the Noldor)
oaths.cite: HoME X, the Annals of Aman §§152-154, year header 1496 [C] — 'from end to end of the hosts of the Noldor the voice was heard speaking the Prophecy of the North and the Doom of the Noldor'. NOT 1495: the OATH is §134 under 1495 and the DOOM is a SEPARATE ANNAL one Valian Year later, with the Kinslaying (§150) still in 1495 between them. Header verified by me.

oaths.when: Y.T. 1496, on the shores of Araman
oaths.q: 'We have sworn, and not lightly. This oath we will keep. We are threatened with many evils, and treason not least; but one thing is not said: that we shall suffer from cowardice, from cravens or the fear of cravens. Therefore I say that we will go on, and this doom I add: the deeds that we shall do shall be the matter of song until the last days of Arda.'
oaths.name: Fëanor's answer to the Doom
oaths.cite: Silm 9 for the words [C]; AAm 1496 (HoME X) [C] for the YEAR AND THE WORDS — the Annals of Aman carry this speech verbatim: 'We have sworn, and not lightly. This oath we will keep. We are threatened with many evils, and treason not least'. Header verified by me at 1496. THE ANNALS OF AMAN HAVE NO ENTRY IN map/annal_header.py's SECTIONS, so the bound was established by hand from the file's own headings — lines 1898-5415 of t1_10_morgoths_ring.txt, from the second 'THE ANNALS OF AMAN' to the line before 'THE LATER QUENTA SILMARILLION' — and that is stated because a bound nobody names is a bound nobody can verify

oaths.q: 'Thou speakest of thraldom. If thraldom it be, thou canst not escape it: for Manwë is King of Arda, and not of Aman only. And this deed was unlawful, whether in Aman or not in Aman. Therefore this doom is now made: for twelve years thou shalt leave Tirion where this threat was uttered. In that time take counsel with thyself, and remember who and what thou art. But after that time this matter shall be set in peace and held redressed, if others will release thee.'
oaths.name: The doom of Mandos upon Fëanor: twelve years' banishment
oaths.cite: Silm 7 for the words [C]; AAm 1490 §99 (HoME X) [C] for the YEAR AND THE EVENT — 'Then the Gods were wroth, and they summoned Fëanor before them. And they laid bare all the lies of Melkor; but because it was Fëanor that had first broken the peace and threatened violence in Aman he was by their judgement banished for twenty' — the corpus then reads 'twenty10 years', the 10 being a footnote marker printed into the word, so the quotation stops at 'twenty' rather than being tidied across it; quoted_check refused the tidied form, which is the guard working for the second time tonight on print furniture inside a quotation. Header verified by me at 1490. AND THE TWO TRADITIONS DISAGREE ON THE LENGTH OF THE BANISHMENT: the Annals of Aman say TWENTY YEARS and the Silmarillion says TWELVE — 'for twelve years thou shalt leave Tirion' verifies in Silm and 'banished for twelve' does not verify in AAm at all. The archive quotes the Silmarillion's twelve, which is the published reading; the annal's twenty is recorded here rather than reconciled, because reconciling two witnesses by choosing one silently is the fault this archive is built against. NONE of the record's quoted wording is in the annal — 'Thou speakest of thraldom' and 'Manwë is King of Arda, and not of Aman only' are both absent, so this cite is for the EVENT

oaths.q: 'Yet if it stands but a little while, then out of your house shall come the hope of Elves and Men. This I say to you, lord, with the eyes of death: though we part here for ever, and I shall not look on your white walls again, from you and from me a new star shall arise. Farewell!'
oaths.name: Huor's prophecy to Turgon: 'a new star shall arise'
oaths.cite: Silm 20 for the words as quoted; GA 472 §235 (HoME XI) [C] for the YEAR AND THE WORDS — 'if it stands but a little while,' said Huor, 'then out of thy house shall come the hope of Elves and Men. This I say to thee, lord, with the eyes of death; though here we part for ever, and I shall never look on thy white walls, from thee and me shall a new star arise. Farewell!'. Header verified in the Grey Annals section: 472, one block. The year F.A. 472 was already right; what was missing is that AN ANNAL CARRIES IT — Silm 20 is narrative and the Silmarillion holds no F.A. year anywhere. RECENSION NAMED, per the owner's ruling, and it touches the SPEAKER: the manuscript first gave this speech to HÚRIN and Christopher prints the change — 'said [Húrin >] Huor' — with 'out of [Gondolin later >] thy house' beside it. The archive follows the revised reading, Huor, which is also the published Silmarillion's. The annal's wording differs throughout: 'from thee and me shall a new star arise' against Silm's 'from you and from me a new star shall arise'. AND THE NOTE IS ANNALLED TOO: §237, '[Added subsequently:] And [Glindûr later >] Maeglin, Turgon's sister-son'

oaths.q: 'Yet if it stands but a little while, then out of your house shall come the hope of Elves and Men. This I say to you, lord, with the eyes of death: though we part here for ever, and I shall not look on your white walls again, from you and from me a new star shall arise. Farewell!'
oaths.name: Huor's prophecy to Turgon: 'a new star shall arise'
oaths.cite: Silm 20 for the words as quoted; GA 472 §235 (HoME XI) [C] for the YEAR AND THE WORDS — 'if it stands but a little while,' said Huor, 'then out of thy house shall come the hope of Elves and Men. This I say to thee, lord, with the eyes of death; though here we part for ever, and I shall never look on thy white walls, from thee and me shall a new star arise. Farewell!'. Header verified in the Grey Annals section: 472, one block. The year F.A. 472 was already right; what was missing is that AN ANNAL CARRIES IT — Silm 20 is narrative and the Silmarillion holds no F.A. year anywhere. RECENSION NAMED, per the owner's ruling, and it touches the SPEAKER: the manuscript first gave this speech to HÚRIN and Christopher prints the change — 'said [Húrin >] Huor' — with 'out of [Gondolin later >] thy house' beside it. The archive follows the revised reading, Huor, which is also the published Silmarillion's. The annal's wording differs throughout: 'from thee and me shall a new star arise' against Silm's 'from you and from me a new star shall arise'. AND THE NOTE IS ANNALLED TOO: §237, '[Added subsequently:] And [Glindûr later >] Maeglin, Turgon's sister-son'

oaths.q: 'Yet if it stands but a little while, then out of your house shall come the hope of Elves and Men. This I say to you, lord, with the eyes of death: though we part here for ever, and I shall not look on your white walls again, from you and from me a new star shall arise. Farewell!'
oaths.name: Huor's prophecy to Turgon: 'a new star shall arise'
oaths.cite: Silm 20 for the words as quoted; GA 472 §235 (HoME XI) [C] for the YEAR AND THE WORDS — 'if it stands but a little while,' said Huor, 'then out of thy house shall come the hope of Elves and Men. This I say to thee, lord, with the eyes of death; though here we part for ever, and I shall never look on thy white walls, from thee and me shall a new star arise. Farewell!'. Header verified in the Grey Annals section: 472, one block. The year F.A. 472 was already right; what was missing is that AN ANNAL CARRIES IT — Silm 20 is narrative and the Silmarillion holds no F.A. year anywhere. RECENSION NAMED, per the owner's ruling, and it touches the SPEAKER: the manuscript first gave this speech to HÚRIN and Christopher prints the change — 'said [Húrin >] Huor' — with 'out of [Gondolin later >] thy house' beside it. The archive follows the revised reading, Huor, which is also the published Silmarillion's. The annal's wording differs throughout: 'from thee and me shall a new star arise' against Silm's 'from you and from me a new star shall arise'. AND THE NOTE IS ANNALLED TOO: §237, '[Added subsequently:] And [Glindûr later >] Maeglin, Turgon's sister-son'

oaths.q: 'You say it,' said Morgoth. 'I am the Elder King: Melkor, first and mightiest of all the Valar, who was before the world, and made it. The shadow of my purpose lies upon Arda, and all that is in it bends slowly and surely to my will. But upon all whom you love my thought shall weigh as a cloud of Doom, and it shall bring them down into darkness and despair. Wherever they go, evil shall arise. Whenever they speak, their words shall bring ill counsel. Whatsoever they do shall turn against them. They shall die without hope, cursing both life and death.'
oaths.name: Morgoth's curse upon Húrin and his kin
oaths.cite: CoH 3 (also UT I.ii, Silm 20) for the WORDS [C]; GA 472 §247 (HoME XI) [C] for the YEAR AND THE EVENT — 'Then Morgoth cursed Húrin and Morwen and their offspring and set a doom upon them of sorrow and darkness; and taking Húrin from prison he set him in a chair of stone upon a high place of Thangorodrim'. Header verified in the Grey Annals section: 472, one block; the same annal opens '§217 This is the Year of Lamentation' and carries the Nirnaeth at §219, so the curse and the battle are ONE annal and not neighbours. Corroborated independently by the Later Annals of Beleriand, annal 272 [472] (HoME V) — 'But Húrin would not reveal whither Turgon was gone, and Morgoth cursed him, and he was chained upon Thangorodrim'; 272 is the original year and [472] Tolkien's own emendation as Christopher prints it, and AB 2 calls the battle the FOURTH battle Nirnaith Dirnoth where GA calls it the FIFTH, so that tradition's numbering is the earlier one. THE ANNAL DATES THE EVENT AND NOT THE QUOTATION, which is the division this cite exists to state: the annals carry NONE of the record's wording — 'cursing both life and death', 'the Elder King' and 'cloud of Doom' are all absent from the Grey Annals section, and Morgoth's speech there is a different one, §248 'Sit now there!'. All three volumes cited for the words carry NO year: contains('472') is False in CoH, UT and the Silmarillion alike

oaths.q: 'Sit now there; and look out upon the lands where evil and despair shall come upon those whom thou lovest. Thou hast dared to mock me, and to question the power of Melkor, Master of the fates of Arda. Therefore with my eyes thou shalt see, and with my ears thou shalt hear; and never shalt thou move from this place until all is fulfilled unto its bitter end.'
oaths.name: 'Sit now there' — the binding of Húrin on Thangorodrim
oaths.cite: Silm 20 for the words [C]; GA 472 §248 (HoME XI) [C] for the YEAR AND THE SPEECH, IN THE ANNAL'S OWN WORDING — "'Sit now there!' said Morgoth. 'Look upon the lands where the uttermost woe shall come upon those whom thou hast delivered unto me. Yea, verily! Doubt not the power of Melkor, Master of the fates of Arda! And with my eyes shalt thou see it, and with my ears shalt thou hear all tidings, and nought shall be hidden from thee!'" Header verified by me: 472, one block. THE OPENING SURVIVES VERBATIM — 'Sit now there' — AND THE REST DOES NOT: the Silmarillion's 'where evil and despair shall come upon those whom thou lovest' is the annal's 'where the uttermost woe shall come upon those whom thou hast delivered unto me'. Same speech, two traditions. The setting in the chair is §247, the same annal as the curse itself and as the Nirnaeth

oaths.when: S.A. 3429–3434, at the Stone of Erech
oaths.q: 'Then Isildur said to their king: ''Thou shalt be the last king. And if the West prove mightier than thy Black Master, this curse I lay upon thee and thy folk: to rest never until your oath is fulfilled. For this war will last through years uncounted, and you shall be summoned once again ere the end.'' And they fled before the wrath of Isildur, and did not dare to go forth to war on Sauron's part; and they hid themselves in secret places in the mountains and had no dealings with other men, but slowly dwindled in the barren hills.'
oaths.name: Isildur's curse on the Men of the Mountains
oaths.cite: LotR V.2 for the words [C]. THE YEAR IS THE ARCHIVE'S OWN READING [I-M]: Appendix B DOES annal Aragorn taking the Paths of the Dead — '8 Aragorn takes the Paths of the Dead at daybreak; he reaches Erech at midnight', under March 3019 — BUT THAT IS THE FULFILMENT, NOT THE OATH. The swearing itself, in the Second Age, is not annalled: Appendix B's S.A. entries run 3429, 3430, 3434, 3440, 3441 and none mentions the Men of the Mountains or their oath. Verified by me in Appendix B, bounded by its own headings

oaths.when: T.A. 1964–1975, in the days of Arvedui
oaths.q:
Over the land there lies a long shadow,
westward reaching wings of darkness.
The Tower trembles; to the tombs of kings
doom approaches. The Dead awaken;
for the hour is come for the oathbreakers:
at the Stone of Erech they shall stand again
and hear there a horn in the hills ringing.
Whose shall the horn be? Who shall call them
from the grey twilight, the forgotten people?
The heir of him to whom the oath they swore.
From the North shall he come, need shall drive him:
he shall pass the Door to the Paths of the Dead.
oaths.name: Malbeth the Seer's prophecy of the Paths of the Dead
oaths.cite: LotR V.2 for the prophecy [C]. NO ANNAL [I-M]: 'Malbeth' occurs ZERO times in App B, and so do 'seer' and 'prophec'. The text dates it only relatively — 'in the days of Arvedui, last king at Fornost' — and App A's only Arvedui number is a DEATH date by that appendix's own convention. The archive's span rests on a reign, not an annal.

oaths.q:
Then Fëanor swore a terrible oath. His seven sons leapt straightway to his side and took the selfsame vow together, and red as blood shone their drawn swords in the glare of the torches. They swore an oath which none shall break, and none should take, by the name even of Ilúvatar, calling the Everlasting Dark upon them if they kept it not; and Manwë they named in witness, and Varda, and the hallowed mountain of Taniquetil, vowing to pursue with vengeance and hatred to the ends of the World Vala, Demon, Elf or Man as yet unborn, or any creature, great or small, good or evil, that time should bring forth unto the end of days, whoso should hold or take or keep a Silmaril from their possession.

Thus spoke Maedhros and Maglor and Celegorm, Curufin and Caranthir, Amrod and Amras, princes of the Noldor; and many quailed to hear the dread words. For so sworn, good or evil, an oath may not be broken, and it shall pursue oathkeeper and oathbreaker to the world's end.
oaths.name: The Oath of Fëanor
oaths.cite: HoME X, the Annals of Aman §134, year header 1495 [C] — 'Then Feanor swore a terrible oath. Straightway his seven sons leaped to his side and each took the selfsame oath'. CONFIRMED at Y.T. 1495, header verified by me. The alliterative verse is INSIDE this annal, not a variant beside it.

oaths.when: F.A. 587, after the War of Wrath
oaths.q:
And Maedhros answered: 'But how shall our voices reach to Ilúvatar beyond the Circles of the World? And by Ilúvatar we swore in our madness, and called the Everlasting Darkness upon us, if we kept not our word. Who shall release us?'
   'If none can release us,' said Maglor, 'then indeed the Everlasting Darkness shall be our lot, whether we keep our oath or break it; but less evil shall we do in the breaking.'
oaths.name: 'Who shall release us?' — Maedhros and Maglor on the Oath
oaths.cite: Silm 24 for the words [C]; HoME XI, the TALE OF YEARS [C] for the YEAR — recension A's entry is '597 Maidros and Maglor, last surviving sons of Fëanor, seize the Silmarils. Maidros perishes. The Silmarils are lost in fire and sea', and recension B redates it in one line: '597 This entry was changed to 587'. THE SAME RECENSION, ON THE SAME PAGE, CARRIES THE OWNER'S RULED WAR OF WRATH SPAN: '550–597 The dates of the last war of the Elder Days were changed to 545–587' — so 545 and 587 are the two ends of one redating, which is the witness behind the 31 July ruling. Read at their lines rather than through the tool. THE GREY ANNALS CANNOT DATE THIS: they end at 499. AB 2 gives 397 [597] instead. AND THE ANNAL DATES THE DEED, NOT THE WORDS: the 'Who shall release us?' dialogue is in no annal in any tradition

oaths.q:
Then Fëanor swore a terrible oath. His seven sons leapt straightway to his side and took the selfsame vow together, and red as blood shone their drawn swords in the glare of the torches. They swore an oath which none shall break, and none should take, by the name even of Ilúvatar, calling the Everlasting Dark upon them if they kept it not; and Manwë they named in witness, and Varda, and the hallowed mountain of Taniquetil, vowing to pursue with vengeance and hatred to the ends of the World Vala, Demon, Elf or Man as yet unborn, or any creature, great or small, good or evil, that time should bring forth unto the end of days, whoso should hold or take or keep a Silmaril from their possession.

Thus spoke Maedhros and Maglor and Celegorm, Curufin and Caranthir, Amrod and Amras, princes of the Noldor; and many quailed to hear the dread words. For so sworn, good or evil, an oath may not be broken, and it shall pursue oathkeeper and oathbreaker to the world's end.
oaths.name: The Oath of Fëanor
oaths.cite: HoME X, the Annals of Aman §134, year header 1495 [C] — 'Then Feanor swore a terrible oath. Straightway his seven sons leaped to his side and each took the selfsame oath'. CONFIRMED at Y.T. 1495, header verified by me. The alliterative verse is INSIDE this annal, not a variant beside it.

oaths.when: F.A. 587, after the War of Wrath
oaths.q:
And Maedhros answered: 'But how shall our voices reach to Ilúvatar beyond the Circles of the World? And by Ilúvatar we swore in our madness, and called the Everlasting Darkness upon us, if we kept not our word. Who shall release us?'
   'If none can release us,' said Maglor, 'then indeed the Everlasting Darkness shall be our lot, whether we keep our oath or break it; but less evil shall we do in the breaking.'
oaths.name: 'Who shall release us?' — Maedhros and Maglor on the Oath
oaths.cite: Silm 24 for the words [C]; HoME XI, the TALE OF YEARS [C] for the YEAR — recension A's entry is '597 Maidros and Maglor, last surviving sons of Fëanor, seize the Silmarils. Maidros perishes. The Silmarils are lost in fire and sea', and recension B redates it in one line: '597 This entry was changed to 587'. THE SAME RECENSION, ON THE SAME PAGE, CARRIES THE OWNER'S RULED WAR OF WRATH SPAN: '550–597 The dates of the last war of the Elder Days were changed to 545–587' — so 545 and 587 are the two ends of one redating, which is the witness behind the 31 July ruling. Read at their lines rather than through the tool. THE GREY ANNALS CANNOT DATE THIS: they end at 499. AB 2 gives 397 [597] instead. AND THE ANNAL DATES THE DEED, NOT THE WORDS: the 'Who shall release us?' dialogue is in no annal in any tradition

oaths.name: 'Master of doom by doom mastered' — Niënor's naming of Túrin
oaths.cite: CoH 17 (also Silm 21) for the WORDS [C]; GA 499 §334 (HoME XI) [C] for the YEAR AND THE DEED — 'but she leapt up and ran like a hunted deer, and came to Cabed-en-Aras, and there cast herself over the brink, and was lost in the wild water'. Header verified in the Grey Annals section: 499, one block; GA 499 runs §§320-336 and carries the whole end of Túrin. THE ANNAL DATES THE DEED AND DOES NOT CARRY THE SPEECH, and that is a textual difference rather than a gap: IN THE ANNAL NIËNOR SAYS NOTHING AND FLEES IN SILENCE. Measured across the WHOLE Grey Annals section on three independent distinctive fragments, every one absent — 'turunambartanen' (the squeezed form of turún'ambartanen, checked), 'twice beloved', 'happy to be dead'. The naming is the Narn's, and the record quotes it from there, correctly. The annal's own account of the same moment gives Glaurung the last words instead, §333: 'Hail, Niënor daughter of Húrin. This is thy brother!'

oaths.cite: Silm 15 for the words as the archive quotes them — 'Of the Noldor in Beleriand', where Ulmo speaks them; Silm 23 for Tuor repeating them in Gondolin; GA 116 §111 (HoME XI) [C] for the YEAR — 'Now therefore Turgon prepared to depart from Nivrost, and leave his fair halls in Vinyamar beneath Mount Taras; and then Ulmo came to him a second time and said … Longest of all the realms of the Eldalië shall Gondolin stand against Melkor. But love it not too well, and remember that the true hope of the Noldor lieth in the West and cometh from the Sea'. Header verified in the Grey Annals section: 116, one block. THE `when` READ 'Y.T./F.A. 64' AND BOTH HALVES WERE WRONG. The Y.T. hedge is unnecessary — this is a First Age annal. And 64 is the wrong year twice over: GA 64 §88 is TURGON'S DEPARTURE in the recension Christopher marks 'This annal was later changed to read', and it gives Ulmo no speech at all; Ulmo's FIRST appearance is GA 53 §76, 'In this year Ulmo appeared to Turgon upon the shores of Nivrost', which also carries none of these words. The quoted warning belongs to Ulmo's SECOND coming. RECENSION NAMED per the owner's ruling: the Grey Annals read 'But love it not too well'; the published Silmarillion expands it to 'But love not too well the work of thy hands and the devices of thy heart', which is the form quoted here

oaths.cite: CoH 17 (also Silm 21) for the WORDS [C]; GA 499 §334 (HoME XI) [C] for the YEAR AND THE DEED — 'but she leapt up and ran like a hunted deer, and came to Cabed-en-Aras, and there cast herself over the brink, and was lost in the wild water'. Header verified in the Grey Annals section: 499, one block; GA 499 runs §§320-336 and carries the whole end of Túrin. THE ANNAL DATES THE DEED AND DOES NOT CARRY THE SPEECH, and that is a textual difference rather than a gap: IN THE ANNAL NIËNOR SAYS NOTHING AND FLEES IN SILENCE. Measured across the WHOLE Grey Annals section on three independent distinctive fragments, every one absent — 'turunambartanen' (the squeezed form of turún'ambartanen, checked), 'twice beloved', 'happy to be dead'. The naming is the Narn's, and the record quotes it from there, correctly. The annal's own account of the same moment gives Glaurung the last words instead, §333: 'Hail, Niënor daughter of Húrin. This is thy brother!'

oaths.q:
It is told among the Elves that after Eärendil had departed, seeking Elwing his wife, Mandos spoke concerning his fate; and he said: 'Shall mortal Man step living upon the undying lands, and yet live?' But Ulmo said: 'For this he was born into the world. And say unto me: whether is he Eärendil Tuor's son of the line of Hador, or the son of Idril, Turgon's daughter, of the Elven-house of Finwë?' And Mandos answered: 'Equally the Noldor, who went wilfully into exile, may not return hither.'
    But when all was spoken, Manwë gave judgement, and he said: 'In this matter the power of doom is given to me. The peril that he ventured for love of the Two Kindreds shall not fall upon Eärendil, nor shall it fall upon Elwing his wife, who entered into peril for love of him; but they shall not walk again ever among Elves or Men in the Outer Lands. And this is my decree concerning them: to Eärendil and to Elwing, and to their sons, shall be given leave each to choose freely to which kindred their fates shall be joined, and under which kindred they shall be judged.'
oaths.name: The errand of Eärendil and the judgement of Manwë
oaths.cite: Silm 24 for the words [C]; HoME XI, the TALE OF YEARS, recension C [C] for the YEAR — the entry reads '536 [> 540 > 542] Earendil comes to Valinor', the bracketed chain being Tolkien's own manuscript emendations as Christopher prints them; recension B reports the same movement, 'The date of Ëarendil's coming to Valinor was changed several times, apparently > 536 > 540 > 542', and recension A's original entry is '533 Earendil comes to Valinor'. I read all three at their lines rather than through map/annal_header.py, WHICH RETURNS A WRONG HEADER HERE: its inline pattern requires a digit followed by whitespace and a capital, so '536 [> 540 > 542]' never matches and the entry falls into the previous block — the tool answers 503/533. THE GREY ANNALS CANNOT DATE THIS: they end at 499, inside Túrin's death annal, 'Here the manuscript comes to an end, at the foot of a page, and the typescript also'. AB 2 gives 533 instead, unemended. AND THE ANNAL DATES THE COMING, NOT THE ERRAND: no annal in any tradition carries the errand-speech or Manwë's judgement
